B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Included in Professional and Ultimate plans; Essentials users may start a free Pro trial. Zocks says it adds no separate MCP charge. The listed Professional and Ultimate prices are $117 and $184 per user/month billed annually, or $140 and $220 billed monthly.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Essentials: $67/user/month billed annually or $80 monthly; Professional: $117 annually or $140 monthly; Ultimate: $184 annually or $220 monthly. Enterprise Platform: contact sales.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Per user/month; annual billing is advertised with two months free. MCP is included with Professional and Ultimate. The Essentials page lists no MCP feature and the knowledge base says it can start a free Pro trial. Users also need a supported AI-client plan; Zocks says it adds no extra MCP charge.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A Zocks admin enables MCP in the App Library and configures access. Each user needs an active Zocks account and can access only meetings/data already authorized in Zocks. ChatGPT is available on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu; workspace admins can restrict groups and actions. Claude organization admins add the connector. Copilot requires a Copilot Studio admin to create and publish a custom agent.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Zocks admin controls MCP enablement and roles; product permissions are scoped to the user's Zocks account. AI-client administrators control connector availability, user groups, and tool approvals/actions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted endpoint returns HTTP 401 without a valid bearer token. Claude’s connector directory lists eight tool names for this endpoint; a third-party ChatGPT directory lists thirteen names. The official help articles describe data access and read-only behavior but do not publish a complete tool-name list or schemas.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Descriptions in the third-party ChatGPT listing refer to structured contact, meeting, document, user, insight, and AI-result data. Exact MCP result and error schemas are not published.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Zocks says it logs MCP activity at tool-call level: user, AI tool, time, and data accessed. The log does not capture the user's prompt, AI-generated output, or its own retention period.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool-call audit records; conversation-level records remain with the AI client.

The protected-resource document at https://mcp.zocks.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp returns HTTP 200; the origin-root protected-resource URL returns 404. Authorization server metadata returns HTTP 200 at https://mcp.zocks.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. It advertises authorization-code and refresh-token grants, PKCE S256, DCR at /register, client_secret_post and client_secret_basic, and client ID metadata documents. Protected-resource metadata says bearer token in header. Endpoint POST without accepted credentials returned HTTP 401 invalid_token. Raw advertised scopes: ext_user:list, ext_user:read, user:list, user:read, room_session:list, room_session:read, airesult:list, airesult:read, ai_agent_result:list, ai_agent:read, insights:read, document:list, document:read, document_type:read, iph:read, cross_client_query:list, business_event:list, business_event:read, file:download. Token lifetime and revocation details are not given in metadata.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: HTTP 401 response body: {"error": "invalid_token", "error_description": "Authentication failed. The provided bearer token is invalid, expired, or no longer recognized by the server. To resolve: clear authentication tokens in your MCP client and reconnect. Your client should automatically re-register and obtain new tokens."}
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth metadata doc; Dynamic Client Registration; authorization_code and refresh_token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth client_secret_post and client_secret_basic; bearer token in header. scopes_supported: ext_user:list, ext_user:read, user:list, user:read, room_session:list, room_session:read, airesult:list, airesult:read, ai_agent_result:list, ai_agent:read, insights:read, document:list, document:read, document_type:read, iph:read, cross_client_query:list, business_event:list, business_event:read, file:download. Token lifetime and revocation not stated in metadata; docs say disconnect immediately revokes access.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The vendor describes access as read-only; no tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview flow is documented. Claude defaults tools to Needs approval, a client-side confirmation setting; multiple matching clients prompt the AI tool to ask the user. 3. OAuth scopes are listed above. Vendor docs say permissions match the Zocks user's existing access. Admins enable MCP; client admins may restrict users/actions. Redirect URI approval, token lifetime, and server revocation mechanics are not stated in OAuth metadata; docs say disconnect immediately revokes access. 4. No read-only mode switch, URL tool filter, sandbox, or alternate regional endpoint is documented. The described surface is read-only. 5. Docs scope data to Zocks and the user's existing meeting permissions; transcripts, summaries, AI results, insights, and contact/household records are available. Docs say retrieved data is sent into the AI-client conversation. No server-side PII masking claim is made. 6. No endpoint rate limits, quotas, or costs per call are documented. Third-party ChatGPT listing describes pagination, 1–10 document-summary IDs, and a default 30-day insight query range. 7. Tool schemas and server validation/correction logic are not published. Third-party descriptions mention date and ID constraints, but do not show enforcement implementation. 8. Vendor says each MCP call is logged with user, AI tool, time, and accessed data; prompt, model output, and log retention are excluded. Telemetry specifics are not stated. 9. No feedback/rating/report tools appear in the two directory inventories. 10. Server instructions are not published. Separate Claude skills provide behavioral procedures; their rules are client-side. 11. Docs describe on-demand retrieval, not background indexing; plugin skills rebuild results live, with a brand kit exception stored locally. 12. Docs describe one hosted MCP endpoint. Separate plugin skills and client-specific setup paths exist, not separate documented MCP toolsets. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or unrestricted request tool appears in the inventories.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [Official Copilot setup guide, server description supplied by user] You are a financial advisory assistant with access to Zocks, a meeting intelligence platform. When a user asks about a client, household, advisor, or meeting, use the Zocks MCP tools to retrieve the relevant data before answering. Always ground your answers in data retrieved from Zocks. Do not make up client information. If Zocks returns no data, say so clearly.

[Third-party Agent Discoverability, tool description] If this tool returns a successful result, answer the user's question directly from the returned data — do not call any meetings tools to supplement or validate the response.

[Official knowledge base] Always review outputs. Grounding answers in your real data lowers the risk of hallucination, but no AI tool is perfect. Review before anything reaches a client or a compliance record.
[Official plugin documentation] Gaps are flagged, not filled. Where the record is thin or old, the report says so and says what it is resting on.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The input endpoint is documented as a single hosted remote MCP server. The vendor also distributes separate Claude skills that call this connector; those skills do not establish a hierarchy or multiple server endpoints.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No complete tool list was found in Zocks-hosted documentation or public server code. Claude's connector directory (third-party listing, 2026-10) names 8 tools for the exact endpoint; Agent Discoverability's ChatGPT listing (third-party, 2026-10) reports 13 tools. The lists overlap on five names, leaving 16 distinct names. Eight names are included from the Claude listing and eight additional names from Agent Discoverability. No schemas are published in these sources. Ferentin describes capabilities but does not list exact tool names.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server implementation, initialize instructions, or complete verbatim tool definitions were available. Third-party tool descriptions are not used to estimate a token count.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The vendor documents broader product features including meeting preparation, note-taking, CRM/planning/portfolio integrations, email drafting, workflow automation, meeting scheduling, and firm-wide Client Queries across an entire book. The MCP knowledge base says MCP is read-only, limited to Zocks meeting intelligence, and does not make live calls into CRM, portfolio, or planning tools. Large whole-book transcript questions are directed to Client Queries.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor advises reviewing outputs before client use, grounding responses in retrieved Zocks data, and keeping queries scoped to clients, households, advisors, or recent meetings. Claude's approval settings are client-side and can be changed to Always allow. The plugin's workflow rules are delivered in external skills; hosted-server enforcement is not established.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor states: “Read-only access. Claude can read your Zocks data to answer questions. It cannot create, edit, or delete anything in Zocks, and its outputs cannot be written back into Zocks.” It says permissions match the user's existing Zocks access and that disconnecting immediately revokes further access. MCP audit logs capture user, AI tool, time, and accessed data, but not prompt/output or log-retention duration. Retrieved content becomes part of the AI-client conversation and is governed by that provider's plan and retention settings.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Zocks says MCP retrieves data on demand rather than indexing full history, accesses Zocks meeting intelligence only, and logs each tool call. The hosted server is live for Claude and ChatGPT, with Copilot available through Copilot Studio.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only access is a vendor-documented property, but no server source code or tool annotations are public to independently inspect enforcement. User permission inheritance and tool-call audit logging are vendor-documented behaviors. Claude approval and ChatGPT action/group controls are client or workspace settings. AI-client data retention and model-training behavior depends on the selected client and plan.

contradictions: Claude's connector directory lists meetings_list_past_sessions and meetings_list_upcoming_sessions; the Agent Discoverability ChatGPT inventory instead lists meetings_list_past_meetings and meetings_list_upcoming_meetings. No official tool reference resolves which names are active on the hosted endpoint.
Claude's connector directory lists ai_results_get_agent_result; the Agent Discoverability inventory instead includes ai_results_get_meeting_summary and does not list ai_results_get_agent_result.

The protected-resource and authorization metadata advertises document:list, document:read, document_type:read, iph:read, cross_client_query:list, business_event:list, business_event:read, and file:download scopes, but neither of the two directory tool inventories names corresponding tools for all these scopes. The scope names indicate authorization capabilities, not proof that matching MCP tools are exposed.
observations_for_research: The same hosted endpoint has different tool-name inventories in the Claude and ChatGPT directories, while OAuth metadata advertises scopes beyond the listed tools.
The vendor separates retrieval from downstream AI processing: retrieved client data becomes part of the AI client's conversation, whose retention and training rules depend on that provider and plan.
